The fit gives **Dq ≈ 1986 cm⁻¹** and **B ≈ 573 cm⁻¹**, with C ≈ 2700 cm⁻¹ so that C/B ≈ 4.7.

I fitted the three bands with the `ts_fit_spectrum` tool, pinned to the low-spin regime. The tool's default C (4449) pushed B to its lower bound and gave a poor fit, so I fixed C and iterated until C/B came out at 4.7:

| Fixed C (cm⁻¹) | Fitted Dq (cm⁻¹) | Fitted B (cm⁻¹) | C/B | RMS residual (cm⁻¹) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2820 | 1989 | 585 | 4.82 | 22 |
| 2750 | 1988 | 578 | 4.76 | 19 |
| 2700 | 1986 | 573 | 4.71 | 17 |

The C = 2700 row is the self-consistent solution. The three observed bands are reproduced to within about 20 cm⁻¹ (residuals about −5, −19 and +23 cm⁻¹). With three data points and two unknowns, the fit is only modestly constrained, so treat the values as ±~20 cm⁻¹ in Dq and B.

The tool's band assignments for this solution place the observed bands on the ³E(a), ³T₁(b) and ³T₂(a) / ³A₁ / ³A₂(a) levels from the ³T₁g ground term. I did not verify those assignments independently.
